reports.title: Evergy Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results, Declares Quarterly Dividend and Raises 2026 Guidance

lines: “Given results ahead of expectations driven by strong operational performance and warmer weather, we are increasing our 2026 adjusted EPS guidance range to $4.35 to $4.50 per share from $4.14 to $4.34 per share.

We are also reaffirming our long-term adjusted EPS annual growth target of 6% to 8%+ through 2030 off the original 2026 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint of $4.24, with the expectation that annual EPS growth will exceed 8% beginning in 2028 and through 2030.”
The Company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) guidance range to $4.35 to $4.50 from its original guidance range of $4.14 to $4.34.

Additionally, the Company reaffirmed its long-term adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) annual growth target of 6% to 8%+ through 2030 based on the original 2026 adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) guidance midpoint of $4.24.
The Company expects annual adjusted EPS growth to exceed 8% beginning in 2028 and through 2030.

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS up 27% to $2.58, beat on hot weather and demand growth; 2026 EPS guidance raised to $4.35–4.50
results: Adjusted EPS rose to $2.58 from $2.03, well above the $2.30 estimate; GAAP EPS was $2.59.
Gains came from a hotter summer, recovery of past grid investment through rates, higher underlying demand and more revenue from large customers.
Higher maintenance and depreciation costs held back part of the gain.
Three large customers extended power supply deals, adding about 250MW of load, and a letter of intent was signed with Digital Realty for a 1.4GW project.
Dividend of $0.7225 a share declared; the release does not give quarterly revenue.

guidance.summary: Evergy lifted its 2026 adjusted EPS range to $4.35–4.50 from $4.14–4.34. It kept its target of 6–8%+ yearly adjusted EPS growth to 2030 and expects growth above 8% from 2028.

points: Power plants held up through record peak demand in a very hot summer, the CEO said.
Weather-adjusted demand grew about 4.5% in the quarter, with commercial sales (including data centres) up strongly.
Management expects more large-customer contracts over the next 12–18 months and hopes to sign the Digital Realty deal by mid-2027; serving it could cost about $4bn.
The five-year spending plan is set to grow, with a full update promised in February.
Large-customer tariffs are pitched as keeping bills more affordable for ordinary households.
call.source: Coverage of the 5 Nov 2026 call: T&D World (6 Nov 2026) and Earnings Whispers via Finviz (5 Nov 2026)

watch: Whether the Digital Realty letter of intent becomes a signed power contract.
The updated capital plan in February and how much new shares it may require.
Missouri rate case decision expected in December.
